findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and will fail to instantiate
findings.body: After this PR, MetricAlertDetectorHandler subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler but provides no implementations for its abstract methods (counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and the newly added build_occurrence_and_event_data). Python's ABC machinery will therefore mark MetricAlertDetectorHandler as abstract. Because MetricAlertFire declares `detector_handler = MetricAlertDetectorHandler`, and the Detector.detector_handler property invokes `group_type.detector_handler(self)`, instantiating a Detector whose GroupType is MetricAlertFire will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler with abstract methods ...`. Either implement stub abstract methods on MetricAlertDetectorHandler, or temporarily subclass DetectorHandler (or a non-abstract concrete base) until the abstraction is actually built out.

findings.title: evaluate() docstring still describes a list return
findings.body: The docstring on StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate says: 'Evaluates a given data packet and returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`.' However the signature and body now produce `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]`. Update the docstring to describe a dict keyed by group key, and ideally note that duplicate keys collapse to the last entry (so handlers should never emit more than one result per group_key).

findings.title: evaluate_group_key_value() docstring omits None return path
findings.body: The docstring states the method 'returns a `DetectorEvaluationResult` with the results and any state changes that need to be made', but the signature is `-> DetectorEvaluationResult | None` and the implementation returns None when the dedupe check fails and when `state_data.status == new_status`. The docstring should mention both early-return None cases so callers understand that a None return does not always indicate an error.

findings.title: test_state_results_multi_group passes wrong value for group_2
findings.body: The data packet is built with `{"group_1": 6, "group_2": 10}`, but `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(detector.detector_handler, "group_2", 6, PriorityLevel.HIGH)` is called with `value=6`. Because `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` ignores its `value` parameter when building the IssueOccurrence, the assertion succeeds regardless of which number is passed, and a regression that propagates an incorrect value into the occurrence would not be caught. Pass `value=10` (matching the data packet) and ideally include the value in the mock occurrence so future regressions surface.

findings.title: Detector.group_type property is not cached
findings.body: The new `group_type` property re-invokes `grouptype.registry.get_by_slug(self.type)` on every access. It is consumed both by the `detector_handler` property and by external callers (e.g., tests calling `handler.detector.group_type`). If `detector_handler` is read repeatedly in hot paths (e.g., once per data packet during evaluation), this adds avoidable registry lookups. Consider caching the result on the instance (e.g., via `self._group_type` populated from `self.type` at first access) so each detector instance resolves its group type at most once.
